title: Rajinikanth's Autobiography in the Works, Hints at Tamil and English Release
excerpt: Lyricist Vairamuthu says the superstar told him work is underway and hinted at a bilingual debut — but no publisher or date is confirmed yet.
body:
• Seven-time National Award-winning Tamil lyricist Vairamuthu disclosed on X that superstar Rajinikanth is working on his autobiography, and that the actor hinted at releasing it in Tamil and English simultaneously.
  • Asked directly when the book would come out, Rajinikanth replied: "Work is underway. It will be out soon." — the project is confirmed, but no publisher, title, ghostwriter or release date has been announced.
  • The news surfaced during Vairamuthu's visit to wish Rajinikanth for Jailer 2, which releases on 15 October with a U/A certificate from the CBFC.
  • What this means for you: this would be the first book on his life in Rajinikanth's own voice. Diaspora readers can set a search alert for "Rajinikanth autobiography" on Amazon.in or Flipkart now, so they catch the pre-order listing the moment a publisher and title are announced.

A hint, not an announcement — and that distinction matters

When Tamil lyricist Vairamuthu called on Rajinikanth this week to wish him for Jailer 2, the conversation turned to the one book fans have waited decades for. Posting on X, the poet said the two discussed art and life — and, he pointedly clarified, "did not speak even a single word on politics."

https://x.com/yespunjab/status/2109561124857504252

Then came the update that set fan timelines alight. "I asked him, 'When will your autobiography come out?' To this, he replied, 'Work is underway. It will be out soon.'" Vairamuthu said he told the actor the book was eagerly awaited. "He asked me why and I told him many have a history but you also have charisma," the lyricist wrote.

That is as far as the confirmed news goes. The bilingual angle — behind every headline's question mark — comes from Rajinikanth hinting at the possibility of a Tamil-and-English debut. It is a tantalising hint from a credible source, not a publishing announcement: no publisher, no date, no ghostwriter. Treat it as a possibility the actor raised, not a done deal.

Context & Background

For readers who know the name more than the arc: Rajinikanth — born Shivaji Rao Gaekwad — has been Tamil cinema's defining superstar for half a century, and his origin story is the stuff of legend. Raised in a lower-income family, he worked as a coolie and then as a bus conductor in Bengaluru before film school and a slow, ferocious climb to the top. Biographies exist, including Vaasanthi's 2021 English Rajinikanth from Aleph Book Company — but the actor has never told the story himself.

That is what makes this moment different. A star whose public communication runs through brief statements and rare interviews writing a full autobiography would be a genuine event in Indian publishing. Vairamuthu, one of Tamil cinema's most decorated lyricists, is exactly the kind of figure whose account of such a conversation carries weight.

"He asked me why and I told him many have a history but you also have charisma."

— Vairamuthu, Tamil lyricist, on his conversation with Rajinikanth

Impact & Analysis

A simultaneous Tamil-and-English release would be a deliberate publishing strategy, not a casual choice. Tamil would honour the language and the audience that made him; English would carry the story to the pan-Indian and global readership that now sustains his box office. For a man whose superstardom was built before the social media era — on screen charisma, fan-club culture and a carefully guarded public persona — a memoir is the one format where he controls the narrative completely.

The timing is no accident either. The disclosure lands days before Jailer 2 — Nelson Dilipkumar's sequel to the 2023 blockbuster, CBFC-cleared with a U/A certificate — hits screens on 15 October. An autobiography hint riding the same publicity wave is shrewd: publishers pay attention when an author's face is on every hoarding in the country.

Diaspora Angle

For the diaspora, this could be the rare book launch that crosses language barriers on day one — Tamil-reading parents and English-reading children reading the same story together. Since no title or publisher exists yet, the practical move is to set a search alert for "Rajinikanth autobiography" on Amazon.in or Flipkart today, so the pre-order listing lands in your inbox instead of your feed weeks later. Until then, Vaasanthi's 2021 biography remains the most substantial English-language account of his life.

What's Next

First, the immediate event: Jailer 2 releases 15 October, and every Rajinikanth press interaction around it will now carry a follow-up question about the book. Watch for whether the actor or his team confirms the autobiography on the record, and whether a publisher's name surfaces — the IANS report that broke this story will likely carry any official word first. Until a publisher speaks, the only confirmed fact is the one Rajinikanth gave Vairamuthu: work is underway, and it will be out soon.
